correctness.rationale: ML theoremhood is co-r.e. and non-theoremhood in recursively axiomatizable Skvo is co-r.e., so their intersection is \(\Pi^0_1\). For a fixed strongly aperiodic tileset \(A\), a product \(W\otimes A\) tiles exactly when \(W\) tiles and cannot tile periodically, by coordinate projection and pairing. The primary source's two canonical-formula equivalences then give \(W\) tiles iff the product formula lies in \(\mathrm{ML}\setminus\mathrm{Skvo}\). The construction is effective, so ordinary Wang tileability supplies many-one hardness.

evidence: These results are broader about the individual logics but neither computes the complexity of \(\mathrm{ML}\setminus\mathrm{Skvo}\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: Complexity of an ambient theoremhood set does not determine the complexity of its difference with a recursively axiomatizable sublogic.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 paper proves undecidability of ML and Skvo and obtains one separator from any fixed aperiodic tileset, but it does not classify the entire set difference. Pawlowski classifies ML theoremhood, not the difference. The audited product with a fixed strongly aperiodic factor uniformizes every ordinary tileability instance into a separator while preserving tileability, which is the missing many-one hardness step.

value.rationale: The result upgrades mere proper inclusion and separate undecidability results to a sharp completeness classification of the full logical separation set. That is a natural metalogical invariant with a clear uniform reduction, not an arbitrary special case.
residual_risks: A recursion-theoretic observation applying the same fixed-product aperiodicization may exist outside the indexed logic literature.

final_claim: The set of propositional formulas belonging to Medvedev logic but not Skvortsov logic is \(\Pi^0_1\)-complete under computable many-one reductions; hardness already holds on the canonical formulas obtained by taking an arbitrary Wang tileset product with one fixed finite strongly aperiodic tileset.
limitations: No polynomial-time bound or restricted-variable-fragment completeness is claimed.
